audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows disagreed across layers: phases[4].side Skill vs win[4] Galio, phases[5].side Skill vs win[5] Aurelion Sol, phases[6].side Skill vs win[6] Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: A 49.29% win rate over 637 games is a genuinely even lane, which the full layer's all-Skill tail captured and the content layer contradicted on every one of those rows.
audit.corrected: Level 6 set to Skill on both layers; first item and 2+ items set to Aurelion Sol on both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hero's Entrance was treated as a permanent looming threat with no cooldown named, and spikes[2] built Shadowflame/Stormsurge against report[8]'s Rod of Ages.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180 seconds at rank 1 — the longest cooldown in either kit. A spent ultimate is three minutes of free lane, and that is the actionable half of the spike nobody wrote down.
audit.corrected: 180s and the 4000-unit rank-1 range written into whys[4], spikes[1] and mid; spikes[2] realigned to Rod of Ages.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Galio's PASSIVE a shield ('his shield passive makes short trades bad', 'poke safely behind his passive shield', 'his magic shield absorbs your Q collision damage'). It also never mentions that Shield of Durand taunts.
audit.why: Colossal Smash is an auto-attack reset that deals bonus area damage — there is no passive shield. The shield lives on Shield of Durand (W) and on Hero's Entrance (R). More importantly, Shield of Durand's release TAUNTS nearby enemies at 275 range, and a taunt cancels Breath of Light and Astral Flight outright — both are flagged interruptible. That is the decisive interaction in the lane and it appeared nowhere.
audit.corrected: Passive corrected to an auto-attack reset with the wind-up as the tell; the taunt and its 275 range stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, early and spikes[0].
sources: ownerKit Q and W channel flags

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flagged zero cooldown-sequencing advice; sequencingCues was 0.
audit.why: Every line said 'Justice Punch down' without saying how long down is.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch 11s at rank 1 / 650 range and Hero's Entrance 180s written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and the spikes.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Hero's Entrance' and 'Justice Punch' — both are Galio's real ability names. False positives.
audit.corrected: No change on that basis; the real defect in those strings was the passive-shield error.

edits.before: Hero's Entrance gives him a global surprise-engage threat you can't yet answer
edits.after: Hero's Entrance reaches 4000 units at rank 1, but it is a 180-second cooldown

edits.before: Poke safely behind his passive shield with Winds of War
edits.after: Chip you with Winds of War from 825 while you farm

edits.before: Galio's Winds of War poke plus his magic shield absorbs your Q collision damage while he closes distance with Justice Punch, punishing any greedy charge attempts.
edits.after: Winds of War chips you from 825 while Justice Punch closes 650 into a knockup — and Shield of Durand's release taunts at 275, which ends your channel on the spot.

edits.before: Hero's Entrance lets him teleport in from anywhere on the map for a surprise all-in or a roam-punish, a threat you have no direct answer to before items.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance covers 4000 units at rank 1 and shields his whole team on landing — but at 180 seconds, one spent ultimate buys you three safe minutes.

edits.before: He still threatens flash-ults and roam windows, but your Shadowflame/Stormsurge spike starts giving you the range and burst to out-poke him before he closes in with Justice Punch.
edits.after: He still threatens flash-ults and roam windows, but Rod of Ages gives you the health to eat a knockup, and the black hole clears from outside Justice Punch's 650-unit reach.

edits.before: Galio's shield passive makes short trades bad for you, since his poke gets partially absorbed while your Q needs a clean hit to matter — play patiently, farm from max range, and don't engage into his shield window. His Justice Punch knockup threatens real damage if you're caught close, so keep spacing generous.
edits.after: Colossal Smash is an auto-attack reset, not a shield — the wind-up on his next attack is the cue to step back, not his ability casts. Shield of Durand is the real problem: at 275 range its release taunts you, and a taunt cancels the beam outright. Farm from max range and never let him charge it in your face.

edits.before: Level 6 Hero's Entrance is a global threat that can punish your roams or ambush you outright, so play cautiously and ward flanks even when he seems to be recalling or backing off. This window favors him defensively and offensively both — focus on farming safely and let his kit's lack of sustained damage work in your favor over time.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance covers 4000 units at rank 1 and can punish your roams or land on top of you, so ward flanks even when he looks like he is recalling. But it is a 180-second cooldown — once he spends it on another lane, the next three minutes of mid are yours to farm and stack freely. Track that timer the moment it goes off.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Astral Flight has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 and 650 range — he has no engage at all while it is down. - Shield of Durand taunts on release at 275 range, and that taunt cancels Breath of Light, so never channel in front of a charging Galio. - R is for kill windows.

edits.before: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Justice Punch is 650 range and 11s at rank 1 — with it down he has no way to reach you at all.

edits.before: That’s Galio’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: A charging Shield of Durand means a taunt is coming — do not stand in 275.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by never being inside the 275 he needs: Shield of Durand only taunts what stands next to him, and your beam works from 750.

notes: IMPORTANT — I deliberately did NOT write the flagged interaction 'Your Astral Flight (W) shuts off Galio's Justice Punch (E)'. It derives from a 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag on Astral Flight, but Riot's own description says Aurelion Sol flies OVER terrain — he does not create any. The flag is a tooltip-parse misfire and the same misfire will be feeding this false 'enemy-dash-deniable' interaction into every Aurelion Sol matchup against a dash champion across the whole lane. Worth fixing at the flag level before another agent writes it into a page. Same reason I did not write the 'terrain-cuts-retreat' line about Justice Punch creating terrain.
